dataset.description:
The main task of the doctoral thesis is related to the development of a new diagnostic and monitoring methodology based on the non-destructive testing method (NDT)-acoustic emission (AE). In this context, the main direction is distinguished:
Development of a methodology for accurate and fast diagnostics of material microcracks.
The developed solutions will provide wider practical application opportunities and promote the recognition of the AE method as an effective approach to diagnosing material fatigue microcracks without their physical damage. This will be a significant step in achieving not only energy efficiency, but also industrial and environmental sustainability goals.

Doctoral grant (ID 1141) delivery plan.
1. Research plan, developed chapters of the doctoral thesis:
1.1. Literature, methodologies used and conclusions will be analyzed (June 2025).
1.2. Collect and analyze literature sources, specify the tasks of the doctoral thesis (June 2025 - September).
1.3. Experimental studies with NDT - AE methods. (October 2025 - December)
1.4. Experimental studies with AE equipment Pocket AE-2. (October 2025 - December)
1.5. Analysis and compilation of experimental results. (January 2026 - March)
1.6. Experimental studies with AE equipment AE AMSY-6 Vallen Systeme. (January 2026 - March)
1.7. Preparation of a scientific article for publication Q1/Q2. (January 2026 - March)
1.8. Research results are summarized and formatted, a scientific article is submitted for publication Q1/Q2. (April - May 2026).
1.9. 25% of the doctoral thesis has been completed. (Apr. – Jun. 2026).
2. Publications:
Scientific article submitted for publication in a Q1/Q2 level publication or ERIH (Grant mandatory submission): co-authored by a professor from Texas A&M University, USA, QS WUR 134. (2026.g. Apr. - May}.
Other publication:
1 paper for publication in conference proceedings in Bulgaria. (2025.g. Jul. - Sep.)
Other publication:
1 paper for publication in conference proceedings in Bulgaria. (2026.g. Jan. - March)
3. International cooperation activities/ business trips
Texas A&M University, USA, QS WUR-134. Topic: NDT, AE. (2026.g. Jan. - March.)
4. Completion of semester exams / attestation
5. Preparation of the data management plan for the grant doctoral thesis research in the ARGOS system and submission.

distribution.title:
The doctoral research is planned to implement ideas based on the possibility of monitoring the operability of aircraft and other aviation equipment using non-destructive testing methods, including the acoustic emission method. This method is based on the registration and analysis of acoustic waves that arise during the processes of plastic deformation and destruction (crack growth) of controlled objects. It allows developing an effective defect classification system and objective condition assessment criteria based on the actual impact of the defect on the object.
The main concept of the doctoral research is related to the application of the acoustic emission method to develop a methodology for real-time monitoring and diagnostics of the technical condition of diesel engines, thereby reducing repair and maintenance time. The results of the research will be able to be tested and applied not only to determine the technical condition of diesel engines (in the road transport and maritime transport sectors), but also to determine the technical condition and critical operating time of aviation equipment. The practical implementation of the results of this research will help optimize the monitoring and maintenance of the technical condition of marine diesel engines, as well as aircraft, while simultaneously reducing the associated costs.
